findings.title: A claude transport/credit failure (rc != 0, or a runner timeout) is consumed as a 'rejected output': the message is frozen permanently, the sweep reports SUCCESS, and an outage strands the whole window
findings.evidence: extract() raises ExtractionError for proc.returncode != 0 (auth/credit/529/network), the LIVE-1 loop catches it (:462-464), stamps the attempt budget and freezes after the second call. Reproduced (final-review/probe/repro.py, probe B): claude rc=1 stderr 'Credit balance is too low' -> 2 calls, frozen row, exit 0, receipt {last_success_at set, no error, extraction_failures:[...]}; the post-outage sweep makes ZERO claude calls and files nothing - only a hand edit of extraction-attempts.json un-freezes it (no CLI exists; the digest says 'manual re-run' but names no command). In a fleet-wide outage (the 2026-09-14 meeting-loop 'Credit balance is too low' incident) every filed-eligible message in the window (~10-100) freezes in ONE sweep. A subprocess.TimeoutExpired (runner.py default 120s for the claude call) is the mirror case: attempt stamped, escapes the loop to run()'s catch-all -> exit 3 aborting the rest of the sweep, twice, then frozen. This contradicts the LIVE-1 ruling text and the in-code claim (:428-429 'Run-fatal exit 3 stays for transport ... errors'), the goal STANDING RULE 'fail-closed halts persist the cause' (the SUCCESS receipt is written, so FR-002 gap detection and the FR-009 poller-health line stay green through a dead extractor), and makes run()'s except ExtractionError arm (:852-853) dead code.
findings.spec_ref: FR-002 (run receipt = the artifact gap detection reads), FR-001/FR-005 (at-most-once is about a USABLE result - ledger ruling G2r3-7/LIVE-1), goal STANDING RULES 'Fail-closed halts persist the cause'
findings.recommended_fix: Split the failure classes: raise a distinct ExtractionTransportError for rc != 0 / TimeoutExpired and let it take the existing run-fatal exit-3 path (record_failure, no attempt consumed, next sweep retries), keeping the attempt budget ONLY for parse/schema/quote-gate rejections of an rc-0 result. Add a named un-freeze path (e.g. --retry-frozen or --clear-attempts <source_ref>) and have the digest line name it. Pin with a test feeding rc=1 and asserting exit 3 + receipt.error + zero attempts stamped.

findings.title: A frozen message is re-processed on every sweep: one new frozen ledger row and one duplicate digest line per 10-minute tick, plus two bus reads
findings.file: scripts/brain/client_state_gmail.py:435-455 (freeze branch), :363-365 (no-change check requires `not pending`), :410 (list_open_tasks before the freeze check); scripts/brain/client_state_projections.py:195-204
findings.evidence: A frozen row persists its resolutions as 'partial', so the next sweep re-resolves them to 'pending', skips the G-IDEMP-2 no-change return (it only fires when nothing is pending), enumerates list-tasks (2 shim/bus calls), finds the cache empty and attempts >= 2, and appends ANOTHER frozen row. Reproduced (probe A): rows 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5 across 5 sweeps with 0 claude calls; gmail_section over 24h rendered 5 'extraction failed twice - manual re-run' lines (one per row). At */10 that is 144 rows and 144 digest lines per frozen message per day for as long as it stays in the 3-day window, and the Ledger rewrites the whole JSONL on every append (O(n) per row). Combined with F-1 an outage turns the daily digest into thousands of identical lines (4096-char splits), which is exactly the 'train Josh to skim past the one channel D-03 depends on' failure FR-009 round 2 removed for fireflies refs, and the ~432-re-page pattern FR-003 round 2 removed for escalations.
findings.spec_ref: FR-001 ('WHEN a re-check changes nothing THE SYSTEM SHALL write nothing'), FR-009 (digest legibility / one line per state change), FR-008 (deliberate enumeration - not 288 list-tasks reads per frozen message per day)
findings.recommended_fix: Before enumerating tasks, if the latest same-digest row already carries extraction_attempt.frozen for this identity and the fresh resolution signature equals that row's, return without writing (and without list_open_tasks); keep the receipt's extraction_failures entry so the digest can still surface the frozen set from the receipt (once per day) rather than from repeated rows. Pin with a test asserting sweep N+1 after a freeze appends 0 rows and issues 0 list-tasks calls.

summary: Boundary, lock, escalate-once, identity/cache, tier-1, FR-004/FR-006 guards and the bus guards all hold on code and artifacts (13 claims checked, 3 by my own reproduction probes). Two Critical defects in the LIVE-1 containment: (F-1) a claude transport/credit failure or timeout is treated as a rejected output, freezing every affected message permanently while the run writes a SUCCESS receipt, so an outage strands the whole window with gap detection green; (F-2) a frozen message then appends a new ledger row and a duplicate digest line on every 10-minute sweep (144/day each), violating FR-001's write-nothing rule and flooding the FR-009 digest. Important: poll.ts sits outside the R1 FR-010 allowlist as written (ruled G2r3-9, record not amended), and the live artifacts show the existing comms-backfill writer files the same senders under different contact ids, so FR-006's dedup key will not prevent double rows in the activate goal's parallel run. Note for the orchestrator: in the g4-out copy I read, floor.txt is absent and gate-invocations.json still has G4-matrix/FINAL exits null (expected to be filled after this review).
